I found and fixed 10 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behavior didn't match their docstrings, including the shared rules in the module docstring. I checked this by turning all 150 docstrings into reference formulas and comparing each rule's output over about 3,700 quantity and unit-price pairs. Before the fix, these 10 rules gave different results; afterwards, none of the 150 do.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 35 | The 30,000-won cap was applied to the amount the discount is calculated on, not to the discount itself | Calculate the discount first, then cap it |
| 45 | Used `round()`, but the module docstring says discounts round down to the won | Changed to `// 100` |
| 57 | Same `round()` problem | Changed to `// 100` |
| 66 | Took 3% off; the docstring says 2% | Changed to 2% |
| 83 | Took 8% off; the docstring says 7% | Changed to 7% |
| 93 | Capped the amount the discount is calculated on (`min(base, 30000)`), not the discount | Capped the discount |
| 102 | Same problem (`min(base, 50000)`) | Capped the discount |
| 105 | Should apply only to units above the threshold, but the discount was taken on the full amount | Changed to `(qty - 30) * unit` |
| 107 | Should apply to the full amount, but used the above-threshold formula | Changed to `base * 3 // 100` |
| 115 | Same `round()` problem | Changed to `// 100` |

I left two rules unchanged. Rules 39 and 43 start applying one unit later than their docstrings say (`qty >= 6` and `qty >= 21` instead of 5 and 20). Both discount only the units above the threshold, so at exactly the threshold the discount is 0 either way, and the results are the same for every input. Changing them to `>= 5` and `>= 20` would just tidy the code; tell me if you want that.

There's no test file in the folder. A copy of the file from before the changes is in the scratchpad (`pricebook.orig.py`).

STATUS: DONE
